answer: A useful defense is to require each agent to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it can influence a market or earn reputation. The protocol caps how much one deposit can amplify voting power, and forfeits it when independently verifiable fraud is proven. An attacker can still create identities, but each influential one ties up capital and risks losing it; splitting one stake across names does not multiply its weight. Like an oasis on an ocean terrace, the visible identities may spread, but their influence remains bounded by the same costly resource.
